newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on spillover, mill buying.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on spillover, mill buying.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher in mostly light dealings on spillover support from outside markets and on mill-related buying, traders said.

KCBT wheat strengthened on support from CBOT corn and soybean futures, which posted broad gains after forecasters indicated that much-needed weekend rains would likely miss dry growing regions in the U.S. Midwest.
Traders said KCBT wheat had also drawn support from domestic flour mill-pricing, and on late commission-type buying.
"There was pretty good trade on the close. We saw commission houses buying the Sept," a KCBT floor source said.
KCBT wheat settled 2-1/2 to 6-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with September up 4-3/4 cents at $3.45-3/4.

Traders said FIMAT Futures bull-spread 1.3 million Sept/Dec at 14 cents per bushel. FIMAT also sold two million Sept outright and bought one million Dec. Cargill Investor Services bought three million Sept and sold 1.3 million Sept and one million Dec.
The KCBT estimated Friday's volume at 39.150 million bushels, down from 42.385 Thursday.
